newsitem.title: CANADA: FAA order proposes steep 727 freighter capacity cuts.
newsitem.headline: FAA order proposes steep 727 freighter capacity cuts.

text.p: If the US government safety order governing Boeing Co freighters is implemented as proposed, operators will have 120 days from the effective date to complete required modifications, industry sources said.
The proposed order was published on July 14 and operators have 45 days to comment.
Once a final airworthiness directive is issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration, probably in September, operators of affected aircraft will have to begin reducing payload within 48 hours.

If the upgrades are not completed within 120 days of the effective date, aircraft will have to be operated with a limit of 3,000 pounds per pallet position from the cargo door aft, 2,700 pounds from the door forward. This is a reduction from 8,000 pounds.
This would cut the rated 727 payload to 35,000 pounds from 62,000.
However, most 727 freighters are operated by express companies with low-density payloads.

The FAA said the average payload reported to it by a number of 727 operators is around 45,000 pounds, so the capacity reduction would be a 22 percent cut in effective capacity. The FAA also calls for reducing maximum speed (to 350 from 390 knots).
Industry sources said the FAA is unlikely to change the weight reductions, but could extend time limits.
Strengthening the floor beams is the first phase of the 727 upgrade program proposed by the U.S. regulator. Additional modifications are likely in a followup order next year, the FAA said.
Operators should be able to make floor beam modifications to Boeing 727 floors during routing maintenance, or during weekend layovers, said industry officials.
Hamilton Aviation in Tucson, Arizona, is one of several firms preparing modification kits for FAA certification.

"It is our belief ... that the upgrades to the floor beams that we've designed will be able to be installed within the time frame of a normal C-check", Clayton Hamilton, executive vice-president said..

"We believe this can be done in such a way as to allow the operator to take care of this when the airplane would normally be done in any event, with a maximum of another couple of days added to that particular maintenance check," said Hamilton.

The kits will be issued with instructions so that the actual work could be performed at any FAA-certified work place, he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
